raw_response:
I’ve farmed these 15 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, and at 60 I still make every decision with my own two feet in the mud. I finished high school, so I read fertilizer labels and understand what N-P-K does, but the field is still my real teacher. With just my wife and me, labor is tight, and well water costs electricity that keeps going up. I never start from zero—I look at last year’s notebook and adjust. Fertilizer prices are high this year, but I learned the hard way in 2022 that cutting nitrogen to save 30 yuan per mu cost me 300 yuan in lost wheat yield. I’d rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad harvest.

I keep 12 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the stable income, and 3 mu of Bt cotton because the neighbors to the east made good money on fiber last year at 7.8 yuan per kg. I watch what Zhang and Li do on their similar land—if they change something and it works, I’ll copy it next year, not this year.

For the winter wheat on 12 mu, I will plant an improved Jimai variety at about 12 kg per mu. I will rotary till before sowing because no-till gives me patchy emergence on this soil. Total nitrogen will be 18 kg per mu: 8 kg as basal compound fertilizer, 6 kg urea at jointing in late March, and 4 kg urea at flag leaf. Phosphorus at 6 kg per mu and potassium at 5 kg per mu, all basal. I will irrigate 3 times—overwinter water in November, jointing in March, and grain filling in early May. Two pesticide sprays: one spring herbicide and one fungicide if powdery mildew shows up. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For summer maize on the same 12 mu, I will direct-seed a hybrid within 3 days of wheat harvest using no-tillage—every day delayed costs yield. Seed rate about 2.5 kg per mu. Nitrogen 16 kg per mu, half basal and half at big trumpet stage. Phosphorus 5 kg and potassium 5 kg, both basal. Two irrigations: one at tasseling-silking in late July and one at grain filling in August. Two pesticide applications, one for corn borer and one for aphids or armyworm depending on what shows up. Yield target is 650 kg per mu.

For cotton on 3 mu, I will plough in early April to warm the soil and break compaction. Hybrid Bt seed at 1.5 kg per mu. Nitrogen 14 kg per mu split between basal and first flowering. Potassium 10 kg per mu—cotton is a potassium hog and without it the bolls drop. Phosphorus 6 kg per mu. Three irrigations: seedling establishment, flowering, and boll filling. Six pesticide sprays because even Bt cotton gets aphids and spider mites here. Expected seed cotton yield is 320 kg per mu.

I apply 18 kg N, 6 kg P2O5, and 5 kg K2O per mu for wheat with 3 irrigations and rotary tillage; 16 kg N, 5 kg P2O5, and 5 kg K2O per mu for no-till maize with 2 irrigations; and 14 kg N, 6 kg P2O5, and 10 kg K2O per mu for cotton with 3 irrigations and 6 pesticide sprays.
